title: Understand Their Internal Triggers
coreMove: Respond to a child's device pull by getting curious about the feeling underneath it before imposing a rule.
sourcePressure: The child section applies the discomfort lens to children, asking caregivers to look for urges and uncomfortable states before blaming devices.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would blame screens or diagnose children rather than noticing discomfort and asking better questions.

hook: Understand Their Internal Triggers as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: middle-school swimmer grabbing a tablet after a bad meet
exampleSpecs.audience: parent who wants to confiscate immediately
exampleSpecs.stakes: the disappointment underneath the reach needs language
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent asks what the tablet is helping her not feel before talking about limits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A damp swim cap lies beside a tablet charging cable.

exampleSpecs.domain: eight-year-old avoiding piano practice after a recital mistake
exampleSpecs.stakes: shame may be driving the escape, not laziness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the caregiver points to the recital program and asks which part still feels bad
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A recital program rests beside a piano bench cushion.

exampleSpecs.domain: teen apprentice leaving group project messages unread
exampleSpecs.stakes: anxious uncertainty can masquerade as irresponsibility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mentor asks what part of opening the thread feels worst before setting the response plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A shop apron hangs beside an unread project thread.

exampleSpecs.domain: child in a hospital waiting room reaching for games
exampleSpecs.audience: grandparent assuming boredom is the whole story
exampleSpecs.stakes: fear may need naming before distraction rules make sense
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the grandparent asks whether the game is for boredom or worry and waits through the pause
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A paper wristband lies next to a handheld game case.

exampleSpecs.domain: young chess player disappearing into videos after a tournament loss
exampleSpecs.audience: coach helping a child name the trigger
exampleSpecs.stakes: loss recovery teaches attention better than a lecture
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach reviews the scoresheet and asks what the video made him not think about
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A chess scoresheet sits beside a captured-piece pouch.

exampleSpecs.domain: sibling pair fighting over a shared console after moving homes
exampleSpecs.audience: parent seeing conflict as device obsession
exampleSpecs.stakes: loneliness and instability may sit under the fight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, the parent sets a rule only; after, the parent asks what changed after the move that makes the console feel important
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A moving-box label sticks to a console controller case.
